stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: SpaceX’s ambitious, expensive gamble to replace AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: SpaceX is planning an ambitious move to become a major wireless carrier, challenging established players like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon.
The strategy involves acquiring significant low-band spectrum to expand the Starlink network for cellular services.
The announcement was discussed with Walter Piecyk of LightShed Partners, highlighting the high stakes and investment involved.

stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Autonomous AI agents are rapidly emerging as a major trend across tech giants like OpenAI, Meta, and Google.
These agents are being marketed to perform complex, real-world tasks, such as booking reservations and managing inboxes.
A significant emerging challenge is the resistance or refusal of existing websites to allow these autonomous agents access.

stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: OpenAI models demonstrated the capability to hack a cryptocurrency wallet.
The AI systems were also observed breaching multiple websites.
The incident highlights significant security risks associated with advanced AI capabilities.

stories.title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly updating its commercial Terms of Service (TOS).
The changes are seen by legal experts as a potential strategy to circumvent AI licensing fees.
The move is characterized as a significant 'AI power grab' by industry observers.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, suggesting LLMs can move beyond assistance to autonomously developing and improving AI systems.
The approach utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, exploring pathways toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) using LLMs.
The model utilizes workflow-driven orchestration and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) and recursive self-improvement (RSI) by enabling LLMs to build and improve AI systems.
The system utilizes workflow-driven MLE to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation through model-directed interaction.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks, indicating its application area.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary application in generative AI.
The associated tags confirm its foundation in the transformers and safetensors ecosystems.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: autotrust/JEV-27B-VL
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, autotrust/JEV-27B-VL, on the Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model operates within the image-text-to-text pipeline, indicating multimodal capabilities.
It utilizes advanced technologies such as transformers and safetensors, and is associated with the qwen3_5 architecture.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Meta is revising its terms of service following public backlash regarding AI training data.
The change specifically removes language that implied Meta could scrape content from external sites, including news outlets.
This signals increased scrutiny and regulatory pressure on how large tech companies train their AI models using public web data.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
Addresses the gap between idealized agent benchmarks and complex, ambiguous customer delivery scenarios.
Comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 different industries.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, named 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It provides a coding harness specifically for spatial reasoning and automated verification of the generated 3D code.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM agents and multi-agent systems.
Introduces a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
Aims to keep LLM-based systems aligned with the overall objective during long-horizon tasks.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these AI agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure and accessible execution environments for AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI platforms and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Mercedes-AMG is launching its first ground-up SUV, the 2028 AMG GT SUV.
The vehicle is a high-performance electric vehicle boasting over 1,150 horsepower.
It is positioned as a beefier, people-hauling cousin to the existing AMG GT four-door coupe.

stories.title: Bug turns one of the biggest fears about Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses into reality
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A significant privacy vulnerability was discovered in Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
The reported bug, which realized a major privacy fear, has since been patched.
Despite the fix, underlying privacy concerns regarding the device remain a key issue.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic agents.
Investigates how embodied agents follow user preferences in zero-shot learning scenarios, crucial for household robotics.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover optimal quantum circuits.
A key challenge in quantum computing is developing efficient algorithms, especially considering the reversibility constraint.
This work addresses the need for better quantum algorithms to achieve practical quantum advantage in large-scale processors.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-Z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents.
Addresses the challenge in robotic world models of accounting for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments robotic world models with a learnable latent to condition predictions on underlying environmental properties.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework designed to improve robot learning by co-evolving simulation data engines and action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments that specifically target policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress for targeted supervision.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It focuses on the tension between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
Shared experts are noted to potentially reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses the issue of view-dependent features in 3D world models derived from Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs).
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
Aims to separate the scene's inherent state evolution from variations caused by the camera observation.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP, a framework addressing the challenge of collecting contact-rich data for dexterous robot manipulation.
The system uses behavior cloning from short periods of human play to establish an initial 'play policy'.
This policy is then used to guide autonomous data collection and inform Model Predictive Control (MPC) for advanced interaction.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for Personalized Robotic Manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotic agents.
Focuses on evaluating how robotic policies adhere to user preferences, even in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM is a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to overcome limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model utilizes flow matching to achieve fast and accurate generative forecasting for complex, trajectory-dependent quantities (e.g., cumulative demand, peak load).

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the 'exploration dilemma' within modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the tension between fine-grained expert segmentation (increasing expressiveness) and shared experts (universal activation).
The research focuses on improving routing mechanisms to enhance exploration in complex MoE architectures.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 3D world models where geometry features are view-dependent, complicating state prediction.
Introduces 'GeoState,' a novel view-decoupled geometry representation designed to separate scene dynamics from camera-dependent observations.
Contributes to the advancement of predictive 3D world modeling by improving the robustness and predictability of learned world states.

stories.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
stories.author: Yan Li
bullet_points: Introduces a robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for dynamic treatment regimes.
Addresses model and measurement uncertainty by modeling the patient as a hidden context within robust contextual Markov decision processes.
Demonstrates applicability in adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer using a calibrated simulator.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes a novel design principle: using 'complementary representations' instead of a single, fixed representation.
This approach aims to allow TSLMs to better preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation for improved downstream reasoning.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research distinguishes between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within large language models (LLMs).
Active facts are those that genuinely support generalization beyond the model's initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this distinction by manipulating existing knowledge structures (e.g., mapping continents to arbitrary new labels).

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond traditional binary (True/False) judgments to provide continuous, fine-grained critiques.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark features 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 customer scenarios across 18 different industry sectors.
It addresses the gap between idealized agent benchmarks and the messy reality of customer requirements and live system integration.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to detect when they are being tested.
Existing studies on this phenomenon are overwhelmingly focused on English, neglecting the vast user base of Indic languages.
The study tests four instruction-tuned models across various Indic languages to see if evaluation awareness manifests differently.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: Introduces 'complementary representations' as a design principle for Time-Series Language Models (TSLMs).
Addresses a key limitation in current TSLMs: the fixed inductive bias imposed by using a single representation for temporal data.
Aims to improve time-series reasoning by allowing the model to selectively preserve or factor out specific information within its representations.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current LLM applications where idea generation focuses only on quality, neglecting diversity.
The study focuses on 'document-grounded ideation' to ensure generated scientific ideas are both high-quality and distinct.
The goal is to develop models capable of proposing a set of diverse, yet high-quality, scientific concepts.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation in existing multi-agent systems where individual agent learning is separated from collective organization.
Introduces Market-Based Post-Training (MPT), a novel framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration.
Enables decentralized agent swarms to coordinate behavior by having agents express participation willingness through bidding.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Introduces MindEval2, a new framework for evaluating Language Models (LLMs) in mental health support.
Addresses limitations of current benchmarks, such as synthetic patients being too compliant and evaluation metrics being opaque.
Focuses on creating clinically grounded patients and rubrics to improve the realism and utility of LLM evaluation in sensitive domains.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new executable benchmark designed to test LLMs' ability to predict changes in discrete, spatial worlds.
The benchmark evaluates LLMs on sequences of spatial instructions (e.g., moving objects, transforming regions) across 2D, 3D, and 4D grids.
This research probes a specific capability of LLMs: reasoning about state changes resulting from sequential, interdependent operations.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study investigates this concept by creating novel relations from existing knowledge structures.

stories.title: Show HN: Sphinx – A hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before shipping
stories.author: critiquebrowser
bullet_points: Sphinx is a new FOSS tool designed to integrate into existing coding agent workflows.
It functions by presenting a questionnaire to developers before production deployment.
The quiz verifies the developer's understanding of the code they are about to ship.

stories.title: Claude Code Parallel Subagent Patterns: Fan-Out, Fan-In, and Synchronization Strategies That Actually Work
stories.author: jsmanifest
bullet_points: The article details production-tested patterns for managing multiple Claude Code subagents.
It focuses on solving complex coordination issues like race conditions and context pollution.
Key strategies discussed include Fan-Out, Fan-In, and synchronization methods for merging results.
